statement: From a given straight line to cut off a prescribed part.
heath_proof: Let AB be the given straight line; thus it is required to cut off from AB a prescribed part. Let the third part be that prescribed. Let a straight line AC be drawn through from A containing with AB any angle; let a point D be taken at random on AC, and let DE, EC be made equal to AD. [I. 3] Let BC be joined, and through D let DF be drawn parallel to it. [I. 31] Then, since FD has been drawn parallel to BC, one of the sides of the triangle ABC, therefore, proportionally, as CD is to DA, so is BF to FA. [VI. 2] But CD is double of DA; therefore BF is also double of FA; therefore BA is triple of AF. Therefore from the given straight line AB the prescribed third part AF has been cut off.

6.9
**Statement:** From a given straight line to cut off a prescribed part.

**Step 1.** Let AB be the given straight line, and let it be required to cut off one-third of AB. (The method works for any prescribed part 1/n by taking n equal segments in what follows.)

**Step 2.** From A, draw a straight line AC making any angle with AB. [P1]

**Step 3.** Take an arbitrary point D on AC. Using Proposition 1.3, cut off DE equal to AD on AC beyond D, and then cut off EC equal to AD beyond E. Now AC is divided into three equal segments: AD = DE = EC. [1.3]

**Step 4.** Join B to C. [P1]

**Step 5.** Through D, draw DG parallel to BC, meeting AB at G. [1.31]

**Step 6.** In triangle ABC, since DG is parallel to side BC, by Proposition 6.2 the line DG cuts the sides of the triangle proportionally. Therefore AD:DC = AG:GB. [6.2]

**Step 7.** Now DC = DE + EC. Since DE = AD and EC = AD (by construction in Step 3), we have DC = AD + AD, so DC is the sum of two segments each equal to AD. [CN2]

**Step 8.** Therefore AD:DC = AD:(AD + AD). Since DC is twice AD, the ratio AD:DC is as one is to two. By the same proportion established in Step 6, AG:GB is also as one is to two, meaning GB is twice AG. [CN1]

**Step 9.** Since GB is twice AG, we have AB = AG + GB = AG + twice AG, that is, AB is three times AG. [CN2]

**Step 10.** Therefore AG is a third part of AB, that is, AG measures AB three times. Thus from the given straight line AB, the prescribed third part has been cut off. [D5.1]
